title: SOURCE_TARGETS retired: DDL foreign-key restricted SQL does not inherit user pending one-shot state

analysis: checkForeignKeyConstrain uses w.sessPool.Get() to obtain a DDL worker/internal session, then calls ExecRestrictedSQL with ExecOptionUseCurSession on that internal session
ddl/session/Pool.Get marks the pooled session as internal/restricted and does not copy the user session's TxnReadTS or SnapshotInfoschema
ExecOptionUseCurSession here means keep statements on the pooled internal session, not the user session that submitted ALTER TABLE ADD FOREIGN KEY
there is no product-feasible path for SET TRANSACTION READ ONLY AS OF TIMESTAMP in the user session to become pending TxnReadTS in the DDL worker session
source_anchors: pkg/ddl/foreign_key.go:670-727 checkForeignKeyConstrain obtains w.sessPool.Get and uses ExecOptionUseCurSession
pkg/ddl/session/session_pool.go:51-74 Pool.Get configures an internal session and does not import user SessionVars
pkg/ddl/ddl.go:904-906 DDL owns a separate session pool
payload.why_not_execute: A RED would require injecting TxnReadTS directly into the DDL worker session, which would test the harness rather than user-visible product behavior.
payload.next_step: keep as negative cache for the state-ingress generator; prefer candidates where current-session internal SQL runs on the actual user session or an explicitly inherited session state boundary
